title: A common regular hyperplane and twisted cohomology restriction sequences
statement:
Let $k$ be an infinite field [def-weil-field], $n\geq1$, and $E_1,\ldots,E_v$ a finite collection of coherent modules [pqf-def-coherent] on $X=\mathbf P^n_k$. Use twists $E(d)=E\otimes\mathcal O_X(d)$ from [def-pc-projective-space-twist] and module sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology]. There is a nonzero linear form $s=\sum_{j=0}^n a_jT_j\in H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(1))$ such that, for the closed immersion $i:H=V(s)\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], the following hold. There is an isomorphism $H\cong\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$ identifying $i^*\mathcal O_X(d)$ with $\mathcal O_H(d)$ for every integer $d$, with pullback as in [def-pc-module-pullback]. For each $\alpha$ put $G_\alpha=i^*E_\alpha$, which is coherent. For every integer $d$ multiplication by $s$ and restriction give a short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow E_\alpha(d-1)\xrightarrow{s}E_\alpha(d)\longrightarrow i_*(G_\alpha(d))\longrightarrow0.$$
Here $(i_*M)(U)=M(i^{-1}U)$ with its induced $\mathcal O_X(U)$-action. For every $q\geq0$ there is a natural identification
$$H^q(X,i_*(G_\alpha(d)))\cong H^q(H,G_\alpha(d));$$
in particular the associated cohomology sequence has consecutive terms
$$H^q(X,E_\alpha(d-1))\xrightarrow{s}H^q(X,E_\alpha(d))\longrightarrow H^q(H,G_\alpha(d))\longrightarrow H^{q+1}(X,E_\alpha(d-1)).$$
The short exact sequences and the restriction maps are natural in morphisms between the chosen modules, and restriction commutes with multiplying sections by linear forms.

source.place: Tag 08A0 (lemma-exact-sequence-induction), the following remark (remark-exact-sequence-induction) on finitely many modules, Tag 089Z (lemma-hyperplane), and Tag 0EGK (remark-exact-sequence-induction-cohomology). Naturality is for the multiplication and restriction arrows in those sequences.

proof.text: Write $U_j=D_+(T_j)=\operatorname{Spec}A_j$, where $A_j=k[x_\ell\mid\ell\ne j]$ and $x_\ell=T_\ell/T_j$. These opens cover $X$: a homogeneous prime containing all $T_j$ would contain the irrelevant ideal. Each $A_j$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra, so [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] makes it Noetherian. Thus $X$ is locally Noetherian and [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes each $E_\alpha$ quasi-coherent. Put $M_{\alpha j}=\Gamma(U_j,E_\alpha)$; [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-affine-sections-finite] makes it finite, and the counit in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identifies $E_\alpha|_{U_j}$ with $\widetilde M_{\alpha j}$. The frames in [def-pc-projective-space-twist] trivialize every twist on $U_j$; multiplication by $s=\sum a_\ell T_\ell$ is consequently multiplication by $f_j=a_j+\sum_{\ell\ne j}a_\ell x_\ell$ on $M_{\alpha j}$, independently of the twist degree.

source.place: Tag 08A0 (lemma-exact-sequence-induction), first two paragraphs: standard affine charts and multiplication by the affine linear polynomial.

proof.text: Use the coefficient space $V=k^{n+1}$. For every $\alpha,j$ the set $\operatorname{Ass}_{A_j}(M_{\alpha j})$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-primes-finite]. For a prime $\mathfrak p$ in this set, let $W_{\alpha j\mathfrak p}$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak p$ under the $k$-linear map $V\to A_j$, $(a_\ell)\mapsto f_j$. It is a linear subspace, and it is proper: the coefficient vector with $a_j=1$ and all other entries zero maps to $1\notin\mathfrak p$. There are finitely many such subspaces, since both the module collection and the chart collection are finite. Include $\{0\}\subset V$, which is proper since $n+1>0$. Apply [lem-pc-finite-linear-avoidance], using the infinite-field hypothesis, to choose a vector outside their union. It gives a nonzero linear form $s$ and $f_j\notin\mathfrak p$ for every listed prime. Including $\{0\}$ also handles an empty module collection or zero modules without requiring their associated-prime sets to be nonempty.

source.place: Tag 08A0 (lemma-exact-sequence-induction), associated-prime avoidance paragraph, and remark-exact-sequence-induction: apply avoidance simultaneously to all modules and all charts.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-module-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes], each chosen $f_j$ is a nonzerodivisor on every $M_{\alpha j}$: $f_jm=0$ implies $m=0$. This remains injective on every localization $(M_{\alpha j})_r$. Indeed, if $f_j(m/r^b)=0$, then $r^c f_jm=0$ for some $c$, hence $r^cm=0$ by injectivity on $M_{\alpha j}$, so $m/r^b=0$. Under the principal-open descriptions of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] and the counit of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], these are exactly the multiplication maps on a basis of opens of each $U_j$. Therefore their sheaf kernels vanish. Since the $U_j$ cover $X$, multiplication $E_\alpha(-1)\xrightarrow{s}E_\alpha$ is injective for every $\alpha$. The same local calculation proves injectivity $E_\alpha(d-1)\xrightarrow{s}E_\alpha(d)$ for every integer $d$.

source.place: Tag 08A0 (lemma-exact-sequence-induction), injectivity using Algebra Tag 00LD (lemma-ass-zero-divisors); localization argument written out.

proof.text:
Let $S=k[T_0,\ldots,T_n]$ with its usual grading. The graded quotient $S\twoheadrightarrow S/(s)$ gives a closed immersion $\operatorname{Proj}(S/(s))\to X$ by [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality]. On $U_j$ its ring map is the quotient $A_j\to A_j/(f_j)$: taking degree-zero fractions after inverting $T_j$ makes $s$ equal to $T_j f_j$. Thus this closed immersion is exactly the zero subscheme $i:H=V(s)\hookrightarrow X$, with the local quotient description of [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Reindex coordinates so that $a_n\ne0$. The maps
$$k[S_0,\ldots,S_{n-1}]\longrightarrow S/(s),\quad S_j\longmapsto\overline T_j,$$
and the map in the other direction with $\overline T_j\mapsto S_j$ for $j<n$ and $\overline T_n\mapsto-a_n^{-1}\sum_{j<n}a_jS_j$ are inverse graded maps. The graded-isomorphism clause of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] therefore identifies $H$ with $\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$. On its standard chart indexed by $j<n$, this identification sends $S_\ell/S_j$ to $T_\ell/T_j$.

source.place: Tag 089Z (lemma-hyperplane), proof: quotient by the linear form, elimination of a variable, and functoriality of Proj.

proof.text: The charts with $j<n$ cover $H$: in $S/(s)$ the relation expresses $T_n$ as a linear combination of $T_0,\ldots,T_{n-1}$, so these elements generate the irrelevant ideal. On their intersections, the pulled-back frames of $\mathcal O_X(d)$ have transition $(T_j/T_\ell)^d=(S_j/S_\ell)^d$. The definition [def-pc-projective-space-twist] identifies this glued invertible module with $\mathcal O_H(d)$ for every $d\in\mathbf Z$, including negative degrees. Put $G_\alpha=i^*E_\alpha$. It is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. The natural affine pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] describes it on $H\cap U_j=\operatorname{Spec}(A_j/(f_j))$ by $M_{\alpha j}\otimes_{A_j}A_j/(f_j)$. If $m_1,\ldots,m_b$ generate $M_{\alpha j}$, the elements $m_t\otimes1$ generate this tensor product over $A_j/(f_j)$, since $m\otimes c=\sum_t(m_t\otimes1)c_t c$ when $m=\sum_t c_t m_t$. Hence $G_\alpha$ is of finite type. The projective-space charts of $H$ are Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], so [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] proves coherence. The twist $G_\alpha(d)$ is coherent as well, since it is locally isomorphic to $G_\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 089Z (lemma-hyperplane), final assertion on twists; Tag 0EGK (remark-exact-sequence-induction-cohomology); the affine pullback computation supplies coherence of the restricted module.

proof.text:
Fix $\alpha$ and $d\in\mathbf Z$. On $U_j$, trivialize both twists by powers of $T_j$. The multiplication map is $M_{\alpha j}\xrightarrow{f_j}M_{\alpha j}$, with cokernel $M_{\alpha j}/f_jM_{\alpha j}$. The canonical isomorphism
$$M_{\alpha j}/f_jM_{\alpha j}\cong M_{\alpha j}\otimes_{A_j}A_j/(f_j)$$
sends $\overline m$ to $m\otimes1$; its inverse sends $m\otimes\overline a$ to $\overline{am}$, so both maps are well-defined and inverse. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections], this is the affine model of $G_\alpha(d)$, using the restricted twist frame. Its pushforward on a principal open $D(r)\subset U_j$ has sections $(M_{\alpha j}/f_jM_{\alpha j})_r$, by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] on $\operatorname{Spec}(A_j/(f_j))$ and the definition of $i_*$. The associated-sheaf functor preserves cokernels by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]; its quotient arrow here is $m\mapsto m\otimes1$, which is precisely restriction. These identifications commute with localization, and the twist transition units agree by Step 5. They consequently identify the global cokernel with $i_*(G_\alpha(d))$ and its arrow with restriction. Combine this with Step 3 to obtain the asserted short exact sequence for every $\alpha,d$.

source.place: Tag 08A0 (lemma-exact-sequence-induction), cokernel paragraph, and Tag 0EGK (remark-exact-sequence-induction-cohomology): direct affine quotient calculation for all twists.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sc-module-abelian-zariski-cohomology] on $X$ and on $H$: cohomology of any module sheaf agrees canonically and naturally with that of its underlying abelian sheaf. By [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], the latter Zariski cohomology is the cohomology of the underlying topological space. The underlying map of the closed immersion $i$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset, by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Hence [lem-sc-cohomology-closed-immersion-pushforward] applies to the underlying abelian sheaf of $G_\alpha(d)$. Forgetting the module action commutes with $i_*$ directly on every open, because in both cases its sections are $G_\alpha(d)(i^{-1}U)$. Composing the two module-to-abelian comparisons with the inverse of the closed-pushforward comparison gives
$$H^q(X,i_*G_\alpha(d))\cong H^q(H,G_\alpha(d))\qquad(q\ge0).$$
All three comparisons are natural in the coefficient sheaf by their cited statements; the sectionwise forgetting identification is an identity. Thus the resulting comparison is natural, also in degree zero.

source.place: Tag 0EGK (remark-exact-sequence-induction-cohomology), cohomology identification, using the more general closed-topological-immersion comparison of Tag 02UV (lemma-cohomology-and-closed-immersions) and Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree).

proof.text:
The category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules is abelian with enough injectives by [lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], and $\Gamma(X,-)$ is additive and left exact by [lem-sc-global-sections-left-exact]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] applies to each short exact sequence of Step 6. Its right derived functors are exactly the module cohomology functors of [pqf-def-cohomology]. For every $q\ge0$, take the four consecutive terms beginning in $H^q(X,E_\alpha(d-1))$ and use the natural isomorphism of Step 7 on the third term. This gives
$$H^q(X,E_\alpha(d-1))\xrightarrow{s}H^q(X,E_\alpha(d))\longrightarrow H^q(H,G_\alpha(d))\longrightarrow H^{q+1}(X,E_\alpha(d-1)).$$
The second map is the map induced by restriction followed by the comparison of Step 7, as asserted.

source.place: Tag 0EGK (remark-exact-sequence-induction-cohomology), displayed long exact cohomology sequence; derived-functor exact sequence Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors).

proof.text: For a morphism $u:E_\alpha\to E_\beta$, the natural affine pullback identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] turn its restriction into $u\otimes1$. On $U_j$ the squares for the short exact sequences commute because $u(f_jm)=f_ju(m)$ and $\overline{u(m)}=(u\otimes1)(\overline m)$. These equations respect the twist frames of [def-pc-projective-space-twist] and localization, so give the global morphism of short exact sequences. For any other linear form $t=\sum b_\ell T_\ell$, multiplication in these frames is by $g_j=b_j+\sum_{\ell\ne j}b_\ell x_\ell$. The restriction identity is $\overline{g_jm}=\overline g_j\,\overline m$ in $M_{\alpha j}/f_jM_{\alpha j}$; this also holds after localization and therefore on all sections. It proves that restriction commutes with multiplication by linear forms, between the appropriate consecutive twists. Thus both naturality clauses hold for the single $s$ chosen in Step 2.
